questions.question: What do white lines on a roadway do?

options.text: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
Mark a no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Is it safe to follow closely behind a large truck?

options.text: Yes, because you can draft off the truck.
Yes, because other vehicles will move out of the way.
Yes, because other drivers will see you.
No, because you might be in the truck's blind spot where the driver cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because you might be in the truck's blind spot where the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots behind them. If you drive in this area, the truck driver cannot see you. The truck also blocks your view of the road ahead.

questions.question: Before you ride, the fuel valve should be:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before riding, make sure the fuel valve is open. If it is closed, the engine may start but will stall once the fuel in the lines runs out.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by drivers failing to give the right-of-way to motorcyclists.

options.text: One-quarter
More than half
One-half

questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because drivers do not give the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that drivers will yield, even if they must by law.

questions.question: Which check is NOT needed before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Check that your tires have the right air pressure.
Check that the oil level is safe.
Look under the motorcycle for leaks.
Check that the paint is shiny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is shiny.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and tread. Check the oil and fluid levels. Look under the motorcycle for oil or gas leaks. The shine of the paint does not affect safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start to lose control in a curve.
When the motorcycle starts to wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle sticks and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch at the same time. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for the area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which surface is potentially slippery?

options.text: A gravel road
A paved driveway
Dry pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: A gravel road
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement, gravel roads, lane markings, and steel plates or utility covers.

questions.question: Your lane position should do everything except:

options.text: Help other drivers see you.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen, avoids wind blasts and blind spots, and avoids surface hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and apply it again right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and apply it again right away.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the brake pressure. Then apply the brake again with steady, gradual pressure.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery and oily. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to use your headlight and running lights. Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What should a rider do to reduce the chances of a collision?

options.text: Stare straight ahead at your motorcycle.
Refuse to move to avoid a hazard.
Look at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of your motorcycle. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving over bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Stay at a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, maintain a steady speed and ride straight across. Do not zigzag, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: When taking a curve in a group, what formation should you use?

options.text: Single file.
Pairs.
Staggered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single file.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single file when taking curves, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the operator.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They can hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?

options.text: It helps in most situations.
It improves steering.
It causes control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: It causes control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Continue applying the front brake.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during a quick stop, release the brake immediately and then apply it firmly. Use both front and rear brakes together for a quick stop.

questions.question: What should riders do when using a roundabout?

options.text: Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.
Move in a clockwise direction.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Speed up before entering the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection that moves counterclockwise around a center island and has no traffic signal. Enter from the right, yield to traffic already in the roundabout, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your road.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay within the speed limit.
Go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to finish the pass.
Pass more than one vehicle at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete all passes within the legal speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic
Right lane ends
Merge

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic is about to merge ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you traffic laws for that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists must pass one at a time. Wait for each rider to finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared between the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger
Are not required

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests to stay balanced. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling off the bike.
